public_rationale: The September 16, 2025 Senate hearing account records alleged chatbot associations with two suicides [e2]. A complaint available December 11, 2025 alleges a ChatGPT connection to Suzanne Adams’s homicide and Stein-Erik Soelberg’s suicide in August 2025 [e3]. These records establish four distinct reported deaths, including suicide and homicide, before January 15, 2026 [e2, e3]. Wikipedia’s January 14, 2026 revision collected reported chatbot-associated deaths, satisfying the coverage requirement before Marcus’s post [e1].
limitations: The reported associations do not establish that chatbots caused the deaths; the hearing account and complaint record allegations [e2, e3].
The dated Wikipedia revision establishes coverage by January 14, 2026, but does not identify when Wikipedia first began collecting these cases [e1].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: By now there have been several reports of chatbot-associated deaths, both suicides and murders, enough that Wikipedia has started keeping track of them.

statement.excerpt: By now, there have been several reports of chatbot-associated deaths (both suicide and murder), enough that wikipedia has started keeping track.
statement.document_title: A few dark words about chatbots and death

our_interpretation: Read 'several' as at least three distinct reported deaths, with suicide and homicide both represented.
Reported association means a publicly alleged connection with chatbot interactions. It does not require proof that a chatbot caused a death.
Read 'by now' cumulatively through January 15, 2026. The surrounding account begins with deaths reported in 2023, so the target period starts in that year.
Wikipedia tracking means an identifiable article collecting such cases existed by the post date. 'Enough that' does not require evidence of editors' motives.
criteria.support_condition: By January 15, 2026, public records described at least three distinct chatbot-associated deaths, including suicide and homicide, and a dated Wikipedia revision collected such cases.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable historical records establish that the reported cases did not meet the threshold or include both categories, or that Wikipedia began collecting these cases only after January 15, 2026.
